test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 8 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Against which Act did Gandhiji decide to fight and start a Satyagraha?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act (1919)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act was officially known as the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**.
 
• It was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in Delhi on 18 March 1919.
 
• The Act allowed certain political cases to be tried without juries and permitted internment of suspects without trial.
 
• It was seen as a repressive measure and led to widespread anger and discontent among Indians, becoming a catalyst for the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vernacular Press Act (1878)**

 
 
• This Act was enacted by the British government to curtail the freedom of the Indian-language press.
 
• It was introduced by Lord Lytton, then Viceroy of India, and was aimed at preventing the vernacular press from expressing criticism of British policies.
 
• The Act was seen as draconian and was repealed in 1881 by Lord Ripon.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act (1858)**
 
 
• This Act was passed by the British Parliament in response to the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• It marked the end of the East India Company's rule in India and transferred control of India to the British Crown.
 
• The Act provided for the appointment of a Secretary of State for India and established the office of the Viceroy of India.
 
 
 
• **Regulating Act (1773)**
 
 
• This Act was the first attempt by the British government to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India.
 
• It established a system of dual control by the British government and the company.
 
• The Act also created the office of the Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings being the first to hold the position.
